name: Whole address book or call log
plain: A site cannot read your whole contact list, call history or SMS.
meaning: The only contact route is the picker, one chosen entry at a time. No web API reads call logs, SMS, voicemail or calendar events.

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: A site cannot read your whole contact list, call history or SMS.

limits.headline: Can't see your whole contact list, call history or text messages
limits.user_action: Nothing. No browser lets a site do this, even if you tap Allow
can: Ask you to pick contacts one at a time, on browsers that offer a contact picker
Receive only the name, number or email you chose in the picker
cannot: See who you called or who called you
Look at your text messages or voicemail
limits.differs: The contact picker exists only in Chrome on Android. Safari, Firefox and desktop browsers have no way to share contacts at all.

story.what_it_is: A website cannot read your full contact list, call history, texts or calendar. The browser blocks it by design.

marketing.name: Contact Picker API
marketing.pitch: Lets a site ask for one or a few contacts you choose by hand, instead of your whole address book.

story.for_you: You never see a prompt for this, because the option does not exist. If a site wants a contact, you pick the person yourself from a list your phone shows, and the site gets only that one entry.
story.for_makers: Makers who want a friends list, a call log or message history cannot get it from a web page. They either build a native app, use a sign in with Google or Microsoft that shares contacts, or ask people to type or upload names.

use_cases.example: A new social network wants to find your friends on day one. The web version cannot scan your address book, so it asks you to pick a few contacts or import a file.
A web chat app like WhatsApp Web cannot read your phone contacts directly. It syncs them from the phone app instead.
A gift site wants to send a card to a friend. It shows the contact picker so you choose one person and the site never sees the rest.
A browser party game wants to invite friends. It makes a share link you send yourself, since it cannot read your contacts.
A web email or CRM tool imports contacts through a Google sign in permission, not through the browser itself.
A scammy site that wants to harvest your contacts to spam them is stopped, because the web has no way to read the list silently.
A web ride booking page wants to share your trip with a friend. It opens your own messaging app with a link instead of reading contacts.

risks: Native apps can ask for much more
Phishing can still ask you to type contacts

technical_bounds: No SMS send or read (sms: links open the user's app only)
No calendar read (only .ics download or a linked calendar via OAuth)

abuse: Apps that want these must be native or use OAuth APIs

history.change: Picker added; bulk read never offered
